Translation choice: Hebrew elohim can mean God or gods. The ESV makes the serpent's promise likeness to God himself rather than to divine beings.

records.change: "it shall bruise thy head" becomes "he shall bruise"; seed as "offspring"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew pronoun is masculine singular, which the ESV renders as a person. This makes the traditional messianic reading of the verse more explicit, not less.
The Masoretic pointing is the form used for God, which the KJV follows; the ESV reads the same consonants as a plural address to the two angels. Lot is then no longer read as addressing the LORD.

records.change: "provide himself a lamb" becomes "provide for himself the lamb"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew means "for himself", which the KJV's wording leaves open to reading as God providing himself as the lamb. The typology of God providing the sacrifice remains.

records.change: "it shall be seen" becomes "it shall be provided"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew verb is "see"; the ESV renders it by the sense of "The LORD will provide" (v. 8). The KJV keeps the saying about the LORD appearing on the mount.
The Masoretic vowels read shor (ox) and the verb as hamstring; the KJV read shur (wall), as some ancient versions did. A narrative detail, no doctrine.

records.change: "until Shiloh come" becomes "until tribute comes to him"
records.note: The ESV redivides the Hebrew shiloh as shay loh (tribute to him), a reading not in the Masoretic vowels; the KJV keeps Shiloh as a name, long read as a messianic title. The ruler from Judah to whom the peoples submit remains.
Translation choice: Hebrew ratsach is used of unlawful killing, so the ESV narrows the commandment. The KJV's "kill" is broader, which bears on debates about war and capital punishment.

records.change: "her fruit depart" becomes "her children come out"
records.note: Translation choice: the ESV reads the case as premature live birth, while the KJV's wording is usually read as miscarriage. The difference bears on how the law values the unborn child.

records.change: "begotten of thy father" becomes "brought up in your father's family"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew phrase: the KJV reads a half-sister by the same father, the ESV a stepsister raised in the household. It changes whom the law covers.

The ESV follows a Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeut) and the Septuagint's tradition where the KJV follows the Masoretic text. The verse then speaks of the nations allotted to heavenly beings rather than numbered by Israel.

records.change: "unto devils, not to God" becomes "to demons that were no gods"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew: the KJV contrasts the demons with God, the ESV says the demons were not gods. Israel's turning from the true God is still the charge.

records.change: "the lowest hell" becomes "the depths of Sheol"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew is Sheol, which the ESV transliterates and the KJV renders "hell". The verse then reads as the realm of the dead rather than a place of punishment.

records.change: Adds "O heavens; bow down to him, all gods"
records.note: The ESV follows a Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeut) and partly the Septuagint instead of the Masoretic text the KJV translates. The added line is close to the words Hebrews 1:6 applies to Christ.

records.change: "unto them" becomes "upon us"; "fiery law" becomes "flaming fire"
records.note: "Upon us" follows the Septuagint, Syriac and Vulgate rather than the Masoretic "to them"; "flaming fire" reads the obscure esh-dat differently. The KJV's "fiery law" given at Sinai is lost.

records.change: "the LORD shall cover him" becomes "The High God surrounds him"
records.note: The ESV follows the Septuagint here; the Masoretic text, which the KJV follows, has "upon him" and no divine title. God is still the one who shelters Benjamin.

records.change: "they honour God and man" becomes "gods and men are honored"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew elohim can mean God or gods. In Jotham's fable the ESV takes it as plural, so the olive oil honours gods rather than God.

records.change: "an enemy in my habitation" becomes "in distress... envious eye"; God unnamed
records.note: A translation choice for difficult Hebrew: the KJV reads an enemy in God's dwelling, the ESV Eli's house looking on in distress. The ESV also makes the giving passive, so God is not named.

records.change: "fifty thousand and threescore and ten" becomes "seventy"
records.note: The ESV follows a few Hebrew manuscripts and Josephus in omitting the 50,000 that the Masoretic text and Septuagint have. A change of number only.

records.change: "reigned one year" becomes "lived for one year and then became king"
records.note: The Hebrew appears to have lost Saul's age; the ESV renders it literally ("son of a year"), the KJV reads it as the length of reign. No doctrine is involved.

records.change: Torture "under saws" becomes forced labour with saws
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew "put them in/under saws" can mean either. The ESV makes David's treatment of the Ammonites forced labour rather than execution.

records.change: Drops "the brother of": Elhanan kills Goliath
records.note: The Masoretic text lacks "the brother of"; the KJV supplies it in italics from 1 Chronicles 20:5. Without it the verse appears to conflict with David killing Goliath in 1 Samuel 17.
Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the grave or realm of the dead, which the KJV renders "hell" here. The ESV transliterates rather than decide between grave and hell.

records.change: "the LORD will lighten" becomes "my God lightens"
records.note: The Masoretic text repeats the divine name (YHWH); the ESV reads "my God" as in the parallel Psalm 18:28 and some witnesses. God is still the one addressed.

records.change: Statements that David's house falls short become affirming questions
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew can be read as statements or as rhetorical questions. The KJV has David confess his house is not so with God; the ESV has him affirm it, though both keep the everlasting covenant.
The Hebrew has na'arah betulah, "a girl, a virgin"; the ESV leaves betulah untranslated. Her virginity bears on 1 Kings 1:4, where the king did not know her.

records.change: "his ascent" to the temple becomes "his burnt offerings"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew 'olato can mean his ascent or his burnt offering. The ESV reads the sacrifices, as the Septuagint does.

records.change: "Caleb the son of Hur" becomes Caleb's descendants, then Hur's sons
records.note: Translation choice in dividing the Hebrew: the ESV makes Hur Caleb's firstborn (as 1 Chronicles 2:19 and 4:4) rather than Caleb Hur's son.

records.change: "of the father of Etam" becomes "the sons of Etam"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "father of Etam"; the ESV follows the Septuagint's "sons". A genealogical detail only.

records.change: "his wife Hodiah" becomes "the wife of Hodiah"

records.change: "that he had by the spirit" becomes "had in mind"

records.change: Voice heard in every language becomes a voice not heard

records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol. The ESV transliterates instead of rendering it "hell".

records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol. God's presence everywhere is still stated.

records.change: "must shew himself friendly" becomes "may come to ruin"

records.note: The Hebrew has tsaddiq (righteous) and no word for God; the KJV supplies "God" in italics, the ESV reads tsaddiq as a title of God. A translation choice that changes who observes the wicked.

records.change: "deliver his soul from hell" becomes "from Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol, the grave; the ESV transliterates where the KJV renders "hell". A translation choice.

records.change: "The great God that formed all things" becomes "an archer"
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure: rab can mean "great one" or "archer" and meholel "forming" or "wounding". The KJV reads a statement about God; the ESV a proverb about hiring fools, with no mention of God.

records.change: "the people perish" becomes "the people cast off restraint"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew para' means to let loose. The ESV also makes "vision" prophetic revelation, so the proverb is about God's word, not foresight.

records.change: Names "Ithiel" and "Ucal" become "I am weary, O God"
records.note: The ESV redivides and repoints the Hebrew consonants; the KJV follows the Masoretic vowels as personal names. Agur's saying opens as a lament instead of an address.

records.change: "sluices and ponds for fish" becomes "pillars of the land"
records.note: The ESV repoints obscure Hebrew words, reading "pillars" and "wage-earners" where the KJV read weirs and fishponds. A different picture of Egypt's judgment, no doctrine.

records.change: "with hell are we at agreement" becomes "with Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol, parallel to death; the ESV transliterates where the KJV renders "hell".

records.change: "I have chosen thee" becomes "I have tried you"
records.note: The Masoretic text has bachar (chose), which can carry the sense "test"; the Isaiah scroll from Qumran reads bachan (tested). The ESV's "tried" matches the latter.

records.change: "the land of Sinim" becomes "the land of Syene"
records.note: The ESV follows the Dead Sea Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a), which reads Syene (Aswan in Egypt), for the Masoretic Sinim, sometimes taken as China. A place name only.

records.change: "Spirit of the LORD" lifting a standard becomes "wind of the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew allows either reading: the KJV has the enemy come like a flood and the Spirit resist him; the ESV has the LORD come like a stream driven by his wind. A translation choice that removes the Spirit's action.

records.note: Translation choice: the ESV takes Gad and Meni as names of pagan deities, as most scholars do. The KJV translates the words, so the idolatry is less plain.

records.change: "I am married unto you" becomes "I am your master"
records.note: Translation choice for Hebrew ba'al, which can mean husband or lord. The ESV loses the marriage picture of God and Israel that runs through Jeremiah 2-3.

records.change: Title "THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS" becomes "The LORD is our righteousness"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew name has no verb. The KJV makes it a title of the messianic Branch, identifying him as the LORD; the ESV's sentence-name is weaker on that point.

records.change: "a vine in thy blood" becomes "a vine in a vineyard"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads bedameka "in your blood"; the ESV follows an emendation (bekarmeka, "in your vineyard") adopted by many modern versions.

records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol; the ESV transliterates where the KJV renders "hell". A translation choice.

records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol; the ESV transliterates where the KJV renders "hell". A translation choice.

records.note: The Aramaic bar 'elahin can mean "a son of the gods" (a divine being, in a pagan king's words) or "the Son of God"; a translation choice. The KJV's reading is often taken as an appearance of Christ.

records.change: "thrones were cast down" becomes "thrones were placed"
records.note: Translation choice: the Aramaic verb means to throw or set down. The KJV shows earthly thrones overthrown; the ESV shows thrones set for judgment.

records.change: "the Son of man" becomes "a son of man"
records.note: The Aramaic kebar 'enash has no article; the ESV renders it literally, the KJV as a title. Jesus' use of the title in Mark 14:62 draws on this verse.

records.change: "Messiah the Prince" becomes "an anointed one, a prince"; weeks split
records.note: The Hebrew mashiach nagid has no article. The ESV also follows the Masoretic accents, ending the anointed one's coming at seven weeks rather than sixty-nine, which bears on the verse's messianic reading.

records.change: "Messiah... not for himself" becomes "an anointed one... shall have nothing"
records.note: The Hebrew mashiach has no article and we'en lo is literally "and nothing to him"; a translation choice. The KJV's wording points to a vicarious death of the Messiah; the ESV's leaves the figure open.

records.change: "confirm the covenant" becomes "make a strong covenant"; wrath on "the desolator"
records.note: Translation choices in a disputed prophecy; the ESV's wording favours a hostile ruler making the covenant, the KJV's allows a messianic reading. The ESV also has the decreed end poured on the desolator, not the desolate.

records.change: "the God of his fathers" becomes "the gods of his fathers"
records.note: The Hebrew 'elohe can be singular or plural; a translation choice. The KJV implies the king rejects Israel's God, the ESV that he rejects his ancestral gods.

records.change: "utterly take them away" becomes "to forgive them at all"

records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is "between your hands", i.e. on the chest or back. The KJV's wording is often read as foretelling Christ's wounds; the ESV points to a false prophet's self-inflicted cuts.

records.note: The Textus Receptus reads kyrios; Alexandrinus, Vaticanus and others read Iēsous. The ESV reading places Christ at the Exodus, as 1 Corinthians 10:4.

records.change: Omits "wise"; adds "through Jesus Christ our Lord"
records.note: The ESV follows P72, Sinaiticus, A, B and C, which lack "wise" (as in Romans 16:27) and have the added phrases; the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus read as the KJV. Glory is given through Christ rather than to God as Saviour alone.

records.note: The Textus Receptus reads lousanti ("washed"); the critical text reads lusanti ("freed"). Both are by his blood; washing is kept in 7:14.
